payload.title: 40 Wedding Processional Songs to Walk Down the Aisle To
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s planning a destination wedding with a generous budget, choosing the music for the moment they and their wedding party walk in, who want a shortlist they can play to a string quartet, pianist or celebrant, and practical help with timing, separate songs and what to ask an overseas venue about live music and sound.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor about planning a destination wedding (single primary CTA, placed after the destination section); /magazine as a soft secondary link in the close.
payload.angle: Most processional lists are ranked pop playlists with streaming links. This one is built for the aisle itself: 40 songs grouped by style (classical, church and hymns, instrumental, modern), each with a practical reason it works for a walk (tempo, length, how it suits a live player) and who it suits, plus how to time the entrance, split songs between the wedding party and the couple, and what to ask a destination venue about live musicians, outdoor sound, power and music permissions.
must_include: Intro, then exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways
How to choose processional music: timing the entrance to the aisle length; separate songs for the wedding party and the couple; live versus recorded

Four grouped sections of 10 songs (grouped, not ranked): Classical; Church and hymns; Instrumental (processional-specific, linking /expert-advice/instrumental-wedding-songs rather than repeating it); Modern
Each entry: title, composer or artist, a short practical why-it-works for the aisle (tempo, length, live arrangement), and a 'Suits' line
Church entries: any church rule only as an official church source states it, otherwise 'ask your officiant or music director'
Destination angle: live musicians, outdoor sound and power limits, music permissions, all framed as questions for the venue

song_plan.note: Fact batches source each title and composer or artist (and original artist for modern songs) from authoritative pages (publisher, composer or artist official sites, Britannica, hymnary.org, IMSLP, Grove/Oxford, official soundtrack credits). No competitor wedding sites, no Wikipedia, no streaming platforms. Replace any song that cannot be sourced rather than guessing.

avoid: Ranking or numbering as a ranking; 'best', 'top' in body copy
Quoting lyrics; meaning or origin claims unless sourced
Vendor names beyond artists and composers: no cover groups, arrangers, streaming platforms or 'Listen on Spotify' links
Church rules not stated by an official church source
Advisor claims beyond brand-facts.md (single point of contact; works in the couple's time zone; fee and inclusions agreed in writing)
Reusing old-page or competitor wording; any reference to an 'old version' of the page
Gendered 'bride only' framing; the old page assumed a bride walking alone
Research talk in the copy (what we could or couldn't find, sources, method)
Year in the title or dated framing (2024)
